chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn `Ubayd Allah, from Muhammad ibn `Abd Allah, and Musa ibn `Amr, and al-Hasan ibn `Ali ibn Abu `Uthman, from Ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him)

Did Allah know Himself before He created the creation? He (AS) replied: Yes. I asked: Did He see Himself and hear Himself? He said: Allah was not required to do so, because He did not ask Himself or demand anything from Himself. He is Himself, and His Self is He. His Power is effective, and He does not need to name Himself. However, He chose names for Himself for others to call upon Him by, because if He is not called by a name, He is not known. The first thing He chose for Himself was al-`Ali al-`Azim (the Most High, the Most Great), because He is the highest of all things. Hence, His meaning is Allah, and His Name is al-`Ali al-`Azim. That is among His first names because He is High, having elevated above everything.

key_terms.الْعَلِيَّ الْعَظِيمَ: The Most High, the Most Great

ai.seo_question: Did Allah know Himself before creating the universe?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) elucidates the doctrine of divine self-sufficiency, asserting that Allah’s knowledge of Himself is intrinsic and not dependent on sensory faculties like sight or hearing, as He was not yet in need of self-recognition. He further clarifies that names such as al-`Ali al-`Azim were chosen for the benefit of creation to facilitate recognition and invocation, establishing a theological distinction between Allah’s eternal essence and the relational attributes revealed to the cosmos.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 4. My father (RA) said: Ahmad ibn Idris said, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn `Ubayd Allah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Abd Allah; Musa ibn `Amr and al-Hasan ibn `Ali ibn Abu `Uthman, on the authority of Ibn Sinan that I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rid (AS), “Did Allah know Himself before He created the creation?”

He (AS) replied, “Of course.” I asked, “Did He see Himself, and hear Himself?” He said: Allah was not required to do so because He did not ask Himself anything or demand anything from Himself. He is Himself, and His Self is He. His Power was effective and He did not need to call Himself. However, He chose names for Himself so that He could be called upon, because unless He is called upon by His Name, there is no way for Him to be known. Therefore, the first name He chose for Himself was the Most High, the Most Great [al-`Ali al-`Azim], because He is Higher than all things. Hence, His meaning is Allah, and His Name is the Most High, the Most Great. That is among His first names, because He is High, Higher than Everything.
